notes:
Idiom rating: 9.5/10. Round 8 finds the codebase in near-convergence state. Only 1 new P2 finding in the entire pass (email.rs:290 trim_start().to_string() → .to_owned()). No P0/P1 issues found. All prior fix categories confirmed clean: no .unwrap() in library code, no .expect() without invariant comments, no gratuitous clones, no bare return-last-expr statements, no format!("{}") anti-patterns, no .len()==0 tests, no push-loops that should be collect(). The serde_json::from_value(v.clone()) pattern throughout is necessary (from_value takes Value by ownership; args.get() yields &Value). inline std::collections:: paths are P3 style only. ClosureHandler duplication (JMAP-4ii.32) remains an open P1 but is a design issue, not caught-here.
Rust idiom confidence: Converged. Both pass 1 and pass 2 produce only findings at P2+ (the one P2 is a 1-line clippy lint) and P3/P4 (inline std::collections paths, style). No structural idiomatic concerns remain. Codebase can proceed to semantic review.
Maintainer risk: MEDIUM — blob_exists() default-false is a documented footgun but has no compile-time guard; will generate confusing Email/parse behavior in backends that implement parse_email but forget blob_exists. The args panic pattern is pervasive (16 handlers) and panic-isolation via tokio::task::spawn saves data but not user experience.
Confidence: 90% chance of no missed P0 bugs. Least confident flags: blob_exists default behavior (depends on how backends are structured), the args panic pattern (covered by panic isolation). Uncertainty driven by: did not read all test files, did not trace all backend call paths. Would raise confidence if: read tests/memory_backend.rs to verify blob_exists is overridden there.
title: Review: round 8 — jmap-server + jmap-chat-server + jmap-mail-server
